The '''1999 Football Association Charity Shield''' (also known as '''The [[T-Mobile UK|One 2 One]] FA Charity Shield''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 77th [[FA Community Shield|FA Charity Shield]], an annual English [[association football|football]] match played between the winners of the previous season's [[Premier League]] and [[FA Cup]] competitions. The teams involved were [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], who had won both the [[1998–99 FA Premier League|Premier League]] and [[1998–99 FA Cup|FA Cup]] as part of the [[Treble (association football)|Treble]] the previous season, and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], who finished runners-up in the league. Watched by a crowd of 70,185 at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]], Arsenal won the match 2&ndash;1.

This was Arsenal's 15th Charity Shield appearance and Manchester United's 19th. Leading up to the match, both clubs were embroiled in controversy: United withdrew from English football's primary cup competition, the [[FA Cup]], in order to take part in the [[2000 FIFA Club World Championship]]; Arsenal were entangled in a [[Transfer (association football)|transfer]] saga involving their own player, striker [[Nicolas Anelka]], who vowed to never play for the club again. United goalkeeper [[Mark Bosnich]], signed as a replacement for [[Peter Schmeichel]], made the first appearance of his second spell with the club. [[Sylvinho]] started his first game for Arsenal, whereas other signing [[Oleh Luzhnyi]] was named on the substitutes' bench. United went ahead seven minutes before the end of the first half, when [[David Beckham]]'s free-kick hit the underside of the crossbar and narrowly crossed the line before [[Dwight Yorke]] made sure. Arsenal were awarded a penalty in the second half which [[Nwankwo Kanu]] converted and the striker assisted his teammate [[Ray Parlour]] to score the winner.

This result marked Manchester United's first defeat of 1999. It was the second consecutive year that Arsenal beat United to win the Charity Shield. Arsenal manager [[Arsène Wenger]] described it as psychological boost to beat his opponents and felt the win showed that his team were ready for the upcoming season. United manager [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]], on the other hand, believed the defeat highlighted his players needed more game time.

==Background==
[[File:PalmaresManU.jpg|thumb|upright|Manchester United acclaimed a treble of trophies in the 1998–99 season.]]
Founded in 1908 as a successor to the [[Sheriff of London Charity Shield]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Abandonment of the Sheriff Shield |page=11 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=19 April 1908}}</ref> the [[FA Community Shield|FA Charity Shield]] began as a contest between the respective champions of the [[The Football League|Football League]] and [[Southern Football League|Southern League]], although in 1913, it was played between an Amateurs XI and a Professionals XI.<ref>{{cite news |title=The F.A. Charity Shield |page=10 |newspaper=The Times |date=7 October 1913}}</ref> In 1921, it was played by the league champions of the top division and [[FA Cup]] winners for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |title=The Shield: From the beginning |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/first-team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |publisher=Manchester City F.C |date=4 August 2011 |access-date=21 April 2014 }}</ref>{{#tag:ref|The [[Premier League]] replaced the [[Football League First Division]] at the top of the [[English football league system|English football pyramid]] after its inception in 1992.<ref>{{cite news |title=Continental or the full English? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/dec/02/sport.sportfeatures |first=Alex |last=Fynn |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=2 December 2001 |access-date=3 July 2014}}</ref>|group=lower-alpha}} [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] acted as the host of the Shield from 1974.<ref>{{cite news|title=The FA Community Shield history |url=http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |publisher=TheFA.com (The Football Association) |access-date=3 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609184712/http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |archive-date=9 June 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] qualified for the 1999 FA Charity Shield as winners of the [[1998–99 FA Premier League]].<ref name="rule">{{cite news |title=It's time to have a ball |page=128 |newspaper=Sunday Mail |location=Queensland |date=1 August 1999}}</ref> The team overcame close competition from [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] to win their fifth league title in seven years.<ref>{{cite news |title=Glorious United crowned champions |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/345445.stm |work=BBC News|date=17 May 1999 |access-date=9 August 2013}}</ref> In the [[1999 FA Cup Final]], Manchester United beat [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] by two goals to nil and completed the [[Double (association football)|domestic double]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Double joy for Man United |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_cup/350192.stm |work=BBC News|date=22 May 1999 |access-date=8 August 2013}}</ref> The team later went on to win the [[UEFA Champions League]] after defeating [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the season's [[1999 UEFA Champions League Final|final]] and became the first English team to acclaim a [[Treble (association football)|treble]] of trophies in one season.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2010/may/22/bayern-munich-inter-treble-bid |title=Trebles all round to celebrate rarity becoming routine |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |first=Amy |last=Lawrence |date=22 May 2010 |access-date=8 August 2013}}</ref> Given United won both domestic honours, the other Charity Shield place went to league runners-up Arsenal.<ref name="rule"/> United appeared in 18 previous Shields, winning 10 outright ([[1908 FA Charity Shield|1908]], [[1911 FA Charity Shield|1911]], [[1952 FA Charity Shield|1952]], [[1956 FA Charity Shield|1956]], [[1957 FA Charity Shield|1957]], [[1983 FA Charity Shield|1983]], [[1993 FA Charity Shield|1993]], [[1994 FA Charity Shield|1994]], [[1996 FA Charity Shield|1996]], [[1997 FA Charity Shield|1997]]), sharing four ([[1965 FA Charity Shield|1965]], [[1967 FA Charity Shield|1967]], [[1977 FA Charity Shield|1977]], [[1990 FA Charity Shield|1990]]) and losing four ([[1948 FA Charity Shield|1948]], [[1963 FA Charity Shield|1963]], [[1985 FA Charity Shield|1985]], [[1998 FA Charity Shield|1998]]). In contrast, Arsenal won eight previous Shields ([[1930 FA Charity Shield|1930]], [[1931 FA Charity Shield|1931]], [[1933 FA Charity Shield|1933]], [[1934 FA Charity Shield|1934]], [[1938 FA Charity Shield|1938]], 1948, [[1953 FA Charity Shield|1953]], 1998), shared one with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in [[1991 FA Charity Shield|1991]] and lost five ([[1935 FA Charity Shield|1935]], [[1936 FA Charity Shield|1936]], [[1979 FA Charity Shield|1979]], [[1989 FA Charity Shield|1989]], [[1993 FA Charity Shield|1993]]).<ref>{{cite web |first=James |last=Ross |title=List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation (RSSSF) |date=15 August 2013 |access-date=11 January 2014 }}</ref>

The most recent meeting between the two clubs was in the [[1998–99 FA Cup#Semi-finals|FA Cup semi-finals]]; the tie was decided by a replay as the initial game finished goalless.<ref>{{cite news |first=Steve |last=Millar |title=Fergie Fury at Offside Howler |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Football%3A+Fergie+Fury+At+Offside+Howler%3B+Man+Utd+0+Arsenal+0.-a060389139 |newspaper=The Mirror |location=London |date=12 April 1999 |access-date=27 March 2014 }}</ref> The match was settled in [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] when Giggs ran the length of the pitch and evaded several Arsenal players to score the winning goal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Giggs magic sinks Gunners |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_cup/319696.stm |work=BBC News|date=14 April 1999 |access-date=26 March 2014}}</ref> In the close season, Anelka was involved in a protracted [[transfer (association football)|transfer]] saga and vowed to never play for Arsenal again.<ref name="anelk">{{cite news |title= Anelka: The story so far ... |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/405221.stm |work=BBC News|date=2 August 1999 |access-date=8 August 2013}}</ref> He cited the media in England as a reason for wanting to leave the club: "The one thing I can tell you is that I can't stand the English Press, who cause me enormous problems on a personal level,"<ref name="anelk"/> but it was implied that his "gold-digging brothers" wanted Anelka to move abroad to make more money – they served as his [[Football agent|agent]]s.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1999/aug/03/newsstory.sport8 |title=Arsenal snap up Suker to fill the Anelka gap |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |first=David |last=Lacey |date=3 August 1999 |access-date=8 August 2013}}</ref>

In June 1999, United accepted an offer from the FA to withdraw from the FA Cup in order to participate in the [[2000 FIFA Club World Championship]], staged in Brazil.<ref>{{cite news |title=United pull out of FA Cup |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/381662.stm |work=BBC News|date=30 August 1999 |access-date=8 August 2013}}</ref> It was criticised by the new [[Minister for Sport and the Olympics|Sports minister]] [[Kate Hoey]], who suggested the club were treating its supporters in a "shabby way".<ref name="ferg">{{cite news |title=Sir Alex accuses Arsenal 'Cabinet' |first1=Stephen |last1=Wood |first2=Tom |last2=Baldwin |page=1 |newspaper=The Times |date=31 July 1999}}</ref> Manchester United manager [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]] however replied that United had been pressured to make the decision, which aimed to solidify England's [[FIFA World Cup hosts#2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 FIFA World Cup bid]]: "The Government are saying that we should be in the FA Cup, but they are the very people that were saying originally that we have to go to Brazil. They could tell us quite clearly: 'Do not bother about the World Cup bid, leave that to us. It should not be Manchester United's responsibility.'"<ref name="ferg"/>

==Pre-match==
Arsenal manager [[Arsène Wenger]] warned some United players might take a while to get into their stride after last season's exploits: "You will always have a dip when you have been on a high like they have, it takes some time to settle and to understand that you have to fight again. We had players who won the World Cup, the players who won the Double and to get them right psychologically and physically took us some time."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/259565819/?terms=charity%20shield&match=1 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |title=Hoey wilts under United risposte |work=The Guardian |location=London |date=31 July 1999 |access-date=4 May 2021 |page=2 |first1=Daniel |first2=Jon |last1=Taylor |last2=Brodkin}}</ref> Ferguson described the 3–0 defeat in the previous season's Shield as a "humiliation", before discussing how it made the team prepare for the challenges ahead: "I have reminded the players how hard it is to lose when you are playing for United these days – it makes so many other people happy."<ref>{{cite news |title=Ferguson ready for return to familiar hostilities |first=Stephen |last=Wood |page=33 |newspaper=The Times |date=31 July 1999}}</ref> Indeed, United only lost five matches of the whole of last season, with their last defeat coming at home to [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] in December 1998.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal en Real akkoord over Anelka |page=S3 |newspaper=Het Parool |location=Amsterdam |language=nl |date=2 August 1999}}</ref>

==Match==

===Team selection===
Both teams were without several first-team players because of injury problems. Manchester United midfielder [[Roy Keane]] was still suffering from an ankle injury sustained in the previous season's FA Cup final,<ref>{{cite news |title=Big two gear up for Wembley |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/408265.stm |work=BBC News |date=30 July 1999 |access-date=24 March 2014 }}</ref> which meant defender [[Denis Irwin]] took responsibility as the team captain.<ref>{{cite news |title=Parlour gives Gunners Wembley win |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/409273.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=1 August 1999 |access-date=31 May 2020 }}</ref> [[Ryan Giggs]] was also ruled out of the game, though his injury was unspecified.<ref name="inj">{{cite news |title=It's United reserves v Arsenal reserves |first=Alex |last=Montgomery |page=67 |newspaper=News of the World |location=London |date=1 August 1999}}</ref> Forwards [[Andy Cole]] and [[Dwight Yorke]] started upfront for United, in a [[Formation (association football)#4–4–2|4–4–2]] formation where [[David Beckham]] and [[Jordi Cruyff]] acted as the two wide midfield players. Goalkeeper [[Mark Bosnich]], signed as a replacement for [[Peter Schmeichel]], also started, having rejoined the club after a nine-year spell with [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]].<ref name="guard">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1999/aug/02/newsstory.sport4 |title=Arsenal play their troubles away |work=The Guardian |location=London |date=2 August 1999 |access-date=4 May 2021 |first=David |last=Lacey }}</ref>

For Arsenal, defender [[Tony Adams (footballer)|Tony Adams]] was ruled out with injury, as was [[Dennis Bergkamp]], [[Marc Overmars]], and goalkeeper [[David Seaman]].<ref name="inj"/> Anelka did not partake, given his transfer to [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] was on the verge of being completed.<ref>{{cite news |title=Anelka: Is this for real? |first=Norman |last=Fox |page=S1 |newspaper=The Independent on Sunday |location=London |date=1 August 1999}}</ref> New signings [[Oleh Luzhnyi]] and [[Sylvinho]] were both named in the squad, but whereas Sylvinho started the game, Luzhnyi was selected as a substitute. Arsenal, like United, lined up in a 4–4–2 formation. Up front, [[Freddie Ljungberg]] was paired with the club's only available recognised striker, [[Nwankwo Kanu]].<ref name="guard" />

===Summary===
The severe heat meant Manchester United and Arsenal found it hard to find any rhythm early on.<ref name="afp">{{cite news |title=No charity for United as Arsenal sound warning |first=Bill |last=Barclay |page=34 |work=Agence France Presse |location=London |date=1 August 1999}}</ref> Sylvinho fashioned an early chance for Arsenal, though his shot was deflected over. Although midfield pair [[Patrick Vieira]] and [[Emmanuel Petit]] did well to contain their opponents in the opening half-hour, Arsenal's lack of pace and incisiveness upfront was evident – Ljungberg missed three chances before half-time.<ref name="afp"/> Midway through the first half, Beckham was booked by referee [[Graham Barber]] for dissent.<ref name="guard"/> Moments later [[Nicky Butt]] was involved in a brawl with [[Martin Keown]], after the defender nearly caught Butt's face with his boot.<ref name="mirr">{{cite news |title=You've got it all right Arsenal |first=Harry |last=Harris |pages=46–47 |newspaper=The Mirror |location=London |date=2 August 1999}}</ref> Both players were booked for confronting each other, as was Vieira for getting involved.<ref name="mirr"/> United performed better the longer the match went on and scored the opening goal. Beckham's {{convert|30|yd}} [[Direct free kick|free kick]] hit the underside of the crossbar and bounced out; Yorke headed the rebounded ball past goalkeeper [[Alex Manninger]].<ref name="mirr"/> Although replays suggested the goal was Beckham's as his free kick crossed the goal line, it was given to Yorke. Arsenal responded for a short while, but missed "three half-chances".<ref name="ply">{{cite news |title=Arsenal beat Man Utd at Wembley |page=34 |newspaper=Evening Herald |location=Plymouth |date=2 August 1999}}</ref>

Defender [[Jaap Stam]], "nursing an Achilles injury all summer", was substituted in the second half for [[David May (footballer)|David May]].<ref name="guard"/> Arsenal began the half the better of the two teams and Vieira believed he earned his team a penalty in the 49th minute – it was turned down by Barber. The substitution of Sylvinho for [[Luis Boa Morte]] in the 64th minute allowed Ljungberg to play in a natural midfield role.<ref name="ply"/> Two minutes later, Arsenal were awarded a penalty. Vieira, chasing down the ball was adjudged to have his shirt tugged by Irwin in the [[Penalty area|18-yard box]]. Kanu converted the penalty, sending Bosnich the wrong way.<ref name="ply"/> Yorke soon after mistimed his goal effort after being sent clear by Cole.<ref name="ply"/> Substitute [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]] then put Cole through, only for Manninger to produce a one-handed save.<ref name="ply"/> Arsenal scored what proved to be the match winner in the 78th minute. A goal-kick by Bosnich was headed back into United's half by Vieira; Kanu controlled the ball "deftly" and set up Parlour, whose shot went into the net.<ref name="guard"/> [[Teddy Sheringham]] was brought on by Ferguson for Butt with nine minutes of normal time remaining, but with a fourth striker on the field, United were unable to score an equaliser.<ref name="mirr"/> Luzhnyi later came on for Parlour, the final substitution of the match.<ref name="mirr"/>

==Post-match==
{{Quote box |width=25em |quoted=true |bgcolor=#FFFFF0 |salign=left |quote=A defeat is a defeat. But I hope that we have as good a season this season as we did last season after losing to Arsenal in last year's Charity Shield.|source=[[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]], 2 August 1999.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gunner glory as United run ends |first=Mike |last=Collett |page=45 |newspaper=The Advertiser |location=Adelaide |date=3 August 1999}}</ref>}}

The result marked the first time that Manchester United had lost in the calendar year, ending a 33-match unbeaten run.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gunners fire out warning shot |first=Mark |last=Bradley |page=55 |newspaper=Birmingham Evening Mail |date=2 August 1999}}</ref> Wenger believed the result showed that Arsenal were "ready for the season", albeit admitting that the defence had trouble coping with Yorke. He thought it was "...psychologically important to beat United, especially after the great run they have had".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-kanu-ignites-the-gunners-arsenal-2-manchester-united-1-1110158.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-kanu-ignites-the-gunners-arsenal-2-manchester-united-1-1110158.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |title=Kanu ignites the Gunners |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |last=Moore |first=Glenn |date=2 August 1999 |access-date=8 August 2013}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Wenger confirmed afterwards that Anelka would sign for Real Madrid: "I hope everything will be finalised in the next couple of days. In any case, he is not coming back here, and although the contract is not signed yet, I hope it will be after his medical and that is the end of it."<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal in double celebration |page=33 |newspaper=Courier Mail |location=Queensland |date=3 August 1999}}</ref> Kanu, who scored Arsenal's equaliser and set up the match winner, was pleased with his performance and relished the opportunity of establishing himself in the first team, after Anelka's departure.<ref>{{cite news |title=I kan beat them all |first=John |last=Cross |page=51 |newspaper=The Mirror |location=London |date=3 August 1999}}</ref>

Ferguson said the defeat showed that Manchester United needed more games to be ready, "particularly, in the second half" and felt travelling "half way across the world" for [[Season (sports)#Preseason|pre-season]] did not aid their preparation.<ref name="brm">{{cite news |title=Anelka farce real-ly at an end |first=Bill |last=Pierce |page=17 |newspaper=Birmingham Post |date=2 August 1999}}</ref> In terms of the result, he said it was "about as significant" as it was last year.<ref name="brm"/> Bosnich's performance in goal received mixed reviews in the English press; ''[[The Sun (United Kingdom)|The Sun]]'' questioned his positioning and said his kicking was "poor".<ref>{{cite news |title=Reflexes are sharp Bosnich |page=35 |newspaper=The Advertiser |location=Adelaide |date=4 August 1999}}</ref> The player himself assessed: "My kicking has been atrocious and, generally, my distribution from the back has to improve."<ref>{{cite news |title=Bosnich aims to kick weakness into touch |first=Stephen |last=Wood |page=50 |newspaper=The Times |date=3 August 1999}}</ref>
